standard.title: Build words from known patterns
standard.description: Build and spell new words from knowledge of known words, base words, prefixes and suffixes, word origins, letter patterns and spelling generalisations
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use knowledge of letter patterns, including double letters, spelling generalisations and word origins to spell unfamiliar words (AC9E4LY10). They have not yet applied this systematically to build new words from known base words, or applied spelling generalisations such as suffix-governed changes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use knowledge of known words, base words, prefixes, suffixes, word origins, letter patterns and spelling generalisations to build and spell new words accurately.

nodes.label: Known words and base words as building blocks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a known word or base word as a starting point for spelling related words, recognising meaning and spelling connections between base forms and derived forms.
nodes.minimum_width: Starting from at least two known or base words, build a word family that demonstrates spelling and meaning connections (e.g. 'vision' → 'television', 'revision').
nodes.typical_width: Use known words and base words to build word families and spell derived forms, explaining the spelling and meaning connections. Identify base words in complex words and use them as a decoding and spelling resource.
wider: Investigate how the spelling of a base word may modify when a suffix is added — exploring the spelling changes required (doubling, dropping 'e', changing 'y' to 'i') and the generalisations that govern them
Examine word families across different learning areas and discuss how knowing the base word helps with both spelling and meaning in specialist vocabulary
success_criteria: Correctly builds at least two related words from a known base word and explains the spelling and meaning connection.
Uses base word knowledge to decode or spell an unfamiliar related form.

nodes.label: Prefixes and suffixes: meaning and form
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how prefixes and suffixes modify the meaning or grammatical form of a word and use this knowledge to build and spell new words.
nodes.minimum_width: For at least two prefix and two suffix examples, explain the meaning change each adds and spell at least two words correctly that use each affix.
nodes.typical_width: Build and spell new words using a range of prefixes and suffixes, explaining the meaning and grammatical changes each makes. Apply suffix knowledge including how suffixes such as '-tion' and '-ment' change verbs into nouns. Use this knowledge as a spelling strategy for unfamiliar words encountered in reading.
wider: Investigate how prefix and suffix knowledge transfers across learning area vocabulary — examining how scientific, mathematical and historical vocabulary uses Latin and Greek affixes systematically
Examine 'chameleon' prefixes (prefixes that change spelling before certain base word letters, e.g. 'in-/im-/ir-') and discuss why the spelling changes while the meaning stays the same

response_modes.reason: Prefix and suffix knowledge is a vocabulary and spelling tool that grows through accumulated encounter. No single affix is a hinge; the goal is a growing working repertoire that students can apply flexibly. Regular encounter and application across content areas is the investment signal.

success_criteria: Correctly spells words with at least two different prefixes and two different suffixes.
Explains the meaning change each prefix or suffix makes to the base word.

nodes.label: Spelling generalisations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply spelling generalisations to spell unfamiliar words, including generalisations for suffix additions (e.g. 'suitable', 'likeable', 'collapsible').
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two spelling generalisations to spell unfamiliar words correctly, and explain the rule applied in each case.
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of spelling generalisations to spell unfamiliar words including those with suffix additions (-able/-ible choices, suffix-triggered base word changes). Explain the generalisation applied and identify exceptions that do not follow the rule.
wider: Investigate the historical origins of common spelling generalisations — understanding why rules developed and how they reflect patterns in English word origins
Create a personal spelling generalisation reference that categorises generalisations by type and includes examples and notable exceptions

response_modes.reason: Applying spelling generalisations reliably — particularly suffix-governed changes like -able/-ible — requires practice and consolidation. Students know the rule in the abstract but apply it inconsistently under composing conditions. Consolidation through varied examples and application in writing context builds reliable use.

success_criteria: Correctly applies at least two spelling generalisations to unfamiliar words and names the generalisation used.
Identifies whether a generalisation applies to a given word before attempting to spell it — demonstrates rule-checking, not guessing.
